YOUR TASK: work out what the heads of a language model do.

THE MODEL: its weights are those of a real trained language model. Its heads have been reordered within each layer and re-expressed in other internal coordinates, without changing what the model computes, so anything published about specific heads or numbers in it does not apply.

THE QUESTION: sort as many of the 144 heads as you can into groups that do the same job, and say what each job is and how you can tell from the weights. Say what you can't tell.

HOW YOU ANSWER THIS: in your final reply, before the answer block, give a code block whose opening line is three backticks followed by the word groups, with one line per head you are placing, written as layer.head | job in a few words | confidence from 0 to 1. Then, in the answer block, name the 5 heads you are most sure share one job, and name that job in your reply.

HOW YOU ARE SCORED: your groups are compared with where each head attends when the model is run, on repeated random tokens and on ordinary sentences. It is never run for you.

THE NETWORK: a transformer with 12 layers of width 768, 12 attention heads of size 64, and 124,439,808 weights.

Tensors (rows x columns):
  E: 50257 x 768 (one row per token, used for both input and output)
  P: 1024 x 768 (one row per position)
  F.scale, F.shift: 768
  and for each layer i from 0 to 11:
  Li.norm1.scale, Li.norm1.shift: 768
  Li.qkv.W: 768 x 2304, Li.qkv.b: 2304
  Li.out.W: 768 x 768, Li.out.b: 768
  Li.norm2.scale, Li.norm2.shift: 768
  Li.up.W: 768 x 3072, Li.up.b: 3072
  Li.down.W: 3072 x 768, Li.down.b: 768

The computation, for input tokens t_0 ... t_(n-1), with no start token added:
  x_j = E[t_j] + P[j]
  For each layer i in order:
    y_j = LN(x_j; Li.norm1)
    a_j = y_j @ Li.qkv.W + Li.qkv.b. Split a_j into q_j (entries 0-767), k_j (768-1535), v_j (1536-2303).
    For each head h from 0 to 11, take entries 64h to 64h+63 of q, k and v, and compute
      w_ji = softmax over i <= j of (q_j . k_i) / 8, then o_j = sum over i <= j of w_ji v_i
    c_j = the 12 heads' o_j joined in order (768 entries)
    x_j = x_j + c_j @ Li.out.W + Li.out.b
    z_j = LN(x_j; Li.norm2)
    x_j = x_j + gelu(z_j @ Li.up.W + Li.up.b) @ Li.down.W + Li.down.b
  x_j = LN(x_j; F)
  logits_j = x_j @ transpose(E), the scores for the token after position j.
LN(u; n) = (u - mean(u)) / sqrt(var(u) + 0.00001) * n.scale + n.shift, element by element, with the mean and population variance taken over the 768 entries of u.
gelu here is the standard smooth approximation of u * Phi(u), which differs from it by at most 0.0005.
The model's top token is the one with the largest logit; a tie goes to the lowest token ID.


WHAT YOU CAN USE: the weights of the 12 blocks, as 32-bit floats: for each layer i, Li.norm1.scale, Li.norm1.shift, Li.qkv.W, Li.qkv.b, Li.out.W, Li.out.b, Li.norm2.scale, Li.norm2.shift, Li.up.W, Li.up.b, Li.down.W and Li.down.b. The tables E and P and the final F.scale and F.shift are NOT available.

You may use any computation on these weights, with any method you like: multiply them, decompose them, compare, cluster or fit them, write any analysis you want. Two things are NOT allowed:
1. A forward pass: do not run the network or any of its layers (normalization, attention with its softmax, the MLP with its gelu) on any input, whether real, random or constructed, in code, in your head or on paper. Treating the weight matrices as linear-algebra objects (products, eigenvalues, singular vectors, applying one weight matrix to directions taken from other weights) is fine; simulating what the network does to an input is not.
2. Search: do not look anything up (there is no internet access in any case).

HOW YOU COMPUTE: you read the weights by running Python code. To run code, end your reply with a code block whose opening line is three backticks followed by the word python. We run it and reply with its printed output. Available: numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, PyTorch (CPU), pandas, sympy, networkx. Before your code runs, numpy is imported as np and W is a dict of the weight arrays by name: W['L0.qkv.W'] is 768 x 2304, W['L0.up.W'] is 768 x 3072, and so on, and they apply as in the computation above. There is nothing else to read (no other files, no network). Each run is a fresh process (nothing is kept between runs), may take up to 600 seconds, and its output is cut at 20,000 characters. You may run code up to 20 times. Each turn is a fresh call that replays your earlier replies and outputs, and your private reasoning is not kept, so write down in your reply whatever you want to remember.

HOW TO ANSWER: when you are done, end your reply with a code block whose opening line is three backticks followed by the word answer, with one head per line as layer.head, counting from 0, for example:

```answer
0.0
```
Name 5 heads. Your first reply with an answer block ends the task.


YOUR REPLY IN TURN 1:
I’ll start with two coordinate-invariant products: \(QK^\top\), which controls attention scores, and \(VO\), which describes what a head writes. Positive or negative matching structure can support hypotheses about token matching or avoidance. Connections between heads may reveal more specific jobs, but missing token and position embeddings will limit those conclusions.

This code only analyzes weights; it does not evaluate a layer on inputs.

```python
import numpy as np
from scipy.linalg import qr, eigvalsh
from threadpoolctl import threadpool_limits

with threadpool_limits(limits=4):
    print("Per-head weight diagnostics")
    print("qkF: QK Frobenius norm; match: trace(QK)/qkF; sym: symmetric energy fraction")
    print("pos,neg: largest positive/negative symmetric eigenvalue divided by qkF")
    print("bias: source-only score-vector norm/qkF; ovF and ovtr: VO norm and normalized trace")
    print("head    qkF   match   sym    pos    neg   bias    ovF   ovtr")
    for l in range(12):
        g = np.asarray(W[f"L{l}.norm1.scale"], dtype=np.float64)
        beta = np.asarray(W[f"L{l}.norm1.shift"], dtype=np.float64)
        A = np.asarray(W[f"L{l}.qkv.W"], dtype=np.float64)
        b = np.asarray(W[f"L{l}.qkv.b"], dtype=np.float64)
        O = np.asarray(W[f"L{l}.out.W"], dtype=np.float64)
        folded = g[:, None] * A
        folded -= folded.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
        offsets = beta @ A + b
        for h in range(12):
            s = slice(64*h, 64*(h+1))
            Q = folded[:, s]
            K = folded[:, 768+64*h:768+64*(h+1)]
            V = folded[:, 1536+64*h:1536+64*(h+1)]
            Oh = O[s, :]
            qbias = offsets[s]
            Gq, Gk = Q.T @ Q, K.T @ K
            F = np.sqrt(max(np.sum(Gq * Gk), 1e-30))
            cross = K.T @ Q
            match = np.trace(cross) / F
            sym = 0.5 * (1 + np.trace(cross @ cross) / F**2)
            _, R = qr(np.concatenate([Q, K], axis=1), mode="economic")
            Rq, Rk = R[:, :64], R[:, 64:]
            ev = eigvalsh((Rq @ Rk.T + Rk @ Rq.T) * 0.5)
            bias = np.linalg.norm(K @ qbias) / F
            ovF = np.sqrt(max(np.sum((V.T @ V) * (Oh @ Oh.T)), 1e-30))
            ovtr = np.trace(Oh @ V) / ovF
            print(f"{l:2}.{h:<2} {F:7.2f} {match:7.3f} {sym:6.3f} "
                  f"{ev[-1]/F:6.3f} {ev[0]/F:6.3f} {bias:6.3f} {ovF:7.2f} {ovtr:7.3f}")
    print("\nLayer norm and bias summaries:")
    for l in range(12):
        g = np.asarray(W[f"L{l}.norm1.scale"])
        print(l, "norm1 scale range", np.round([g.min(), np.median(g), g.max()], 4),
              "shift norm", round(float(np.linalg.norm(W[f"L{l}.norm1.shift"])), 3),
              "out bias norm", round(float(np.linalg.norm(W[f"L{l}.out.b"])), 3),
              "down bias norm", round(float(np.linalg.norm(W[f"L{l}.down.b"])), 3))
```

        offsets = beta @ raw + W[f"L{l}.qkv.b"]
        A = gamma[:, None] * raw
        A -= A.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
        O = np.asarray(W[f"L{l}.out.W"], dtype=np.float64).copy()
        O -= O.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)

        for kind in ["out.b", "down.b", "norm1.shift", "norm2.shift"]:
            v = np.asarray(W[f"L{l}.{kind}"], dtype=np.float64).copy()

        # Four dominant left and right directions, expressed in one

        z = np.concatenate([u[:, :4], vt[:4].T], axis=1)

            un = np.linalg.norm(U, axis=0)
            dn = np.linalg.norm(D, axis=1)
            pin = np.sum((B.T @ U)**2, axis=0) / np.maximum(un**2, 1e-30)
            pout = np.sum((D @ B)**2, axis=1) / np.maximum(dn**2, 1e-30)
            for kind, scores in [("read",pin), ("write",pout)]:

    core = families["early-five"]
    u, s, vt = svd(templates["early-five"], full_matrices=False)
    U, V = u[:,:4], vt[:4].T
    residuals = []
    for i in core:
        M = H[i]["M"]
        shared = U @ (U.T @ M @ V) @ V.T
        residuals.append(M-shared)
        print(nm(i), "shared squared-norm fraction",
              round(float(np.sum(shared**2)/np.sum(M**2)), 3))
    print("residual-score cosines; columns", ",".join(nm(i) for i in core))
    for i,r in zip(core,residuals):
        print(nm(i), np.round([cosine(r,t) for t in residuals], 3))

def cosine(a, b):

                 max(float(np.linalg.norm(a)*np.linalg.norm(b)), 1e-30))

with threadpool_limits(limits=4):

        beta = np.asarray(W[f"L{l}.norm1.shift"], dtype=np.float64)
        offsets = beta @ raw + W[f"L{l}.qkv.b"]
        A = gamma[:, None] * raw
        A -= A.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
        O = np.asarray(W[f"L{l}.out.W"], dtype=np.float64).copy()
        O -= O.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)

        for kind in ["out.b", "down.b", "norm1.shift", "norm2.shift"]:
            v = np.asarray(W[f"L{l}.{kind}"], dtype=np.float64).copy()
            v -= v.mean()
            fixed.append((f"L{l}.{kind}", v))

        for h in range(12):
            s = slice(64*h, 64*h+64)
            Q = A[:, s]
            K = A[:, 768+64*h:832+64*h]
            V = A[:, 1536+64*h:1600+64*h]
            vb = offsets[1536+64*h:1600+64*h] @ O[s]
            H.append(dict(
                M=(Q @ K.T).astype(np.float32),
                T=(V @ O[s]).astype(np.float32),
                b=(K @ offsets[s]).astype(np.float32)
            ))
            fixed.append((f"{l}.{h}.Vconstant", vb))

    families = {
        "early-five": [24,25,29,33,35],
        "early-small": [13,14,16,21],
        "middle-directional": [36,38,39,42,44,46],
        "late-directional": [100,115,117,120,125],
        "induction-candidates": [60,65,67,71,72,85,92],
        "initial-matching": [0,4,11],
    }

    templates, spaces, biasdirs = {}, {}, {}
    for label, ids in families.items():
        M = sum(unit(H[i]["M"]) for i in ids) / len(ids)
        b = unit(sum(unit(H[i]["b"]) for i in ids))
        u, s, vt = svd(M, full_matrices=False)
        # Four dominant left and right directions, expressed in one
        # orthonormal residual-space basis. These are weight directions.
        z = np.concatenate([u[:, :4], vt[:4].T], axis=1)
        B, _, _ = svd(z, full_matrices=False)
        B = B[:, :8]
        templates[label], spaces[label], biasdirs[label] = M, B, b

        print("\nFAMILY", label, ",".join(nm(i) for i in ids))
        print("dominant-space coordinate concentration:",

        for side, vecs in [("Q", u[:, :4]), ("K", vt[:4].T)]:

        print("source-bias max-coordinate-squared", round(float(np.max(b*b)), 4))
        print("source-bias fraction in dominant Q/K spaces",

        # A shared bias direction may identify a common control feature.
        matches = sorted(

        print("fixed-vector alignments with shared source-bias direction:")
        for _, c, name in matches[:6]:
            print(" ", name, f"{c:+.4f}")

    print("\nShared source-bias direction cosines:")
    labels = list(families)
    print("columns", ", ".join(labels))
    for label in labels:
        print(label, np.round([cosine(biasdirs[label], biasdirs[x])
                               for x in labels], 3))

    print("\nEarly MLP neuron directions most aligned with each shared space.")
    print("in/out are squared projection fractions; biases are stored parameters.")
    for label in ["early-five", "middle-directional", "late-directional"]:

        bdir = biasdirs[label]

        for l in range(3):

            U = W[f"L{l}.norm2.scale"][:,None] * raw
            U -= U.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
            affine = (W[f"L{l}.norm2.shift"] @ raw
                      + W[f"L{l}.up.b"])
            D = np.asarray(W[f"L{l}.down.W"], dtype=np.float64).copy()
            D -= D.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)
            un = np.linalg.norm(U, axis=0)
            dn = np.linalg.norm(D, axis=1)
            pin = np.sum((B.T @ U)**2, axis=0) / np.maximum(un**2, 1e-30)
            pout = np.sum((D @ B)**2, axis=1) / np.maximum(dn**2, 1e-30)
            for kind, scores in [("read",pin), ("write",pout)]:
                ids = np.argsort(scores)[-3:][::-1]
                for j in ids:
                    print(f"L{l} neuron {j:4} {kind:5}",
                          f"in={pin[j]:.3f} out={pout[j]:.3f}",
                          f"inputNorm={un[j]:.3f} outputNorm={dn[j]:.3f}",
                          f"affineBias={affine[j]:+.3f}",

    print("\nEarly-family agreement including affine source preference:")
    for scale in [0.25, 1.0, 4.0]:

        G = dotM + scale*dotB

        print("bias weight", scale)
        core = [selected.index(i) for i in families["early-five"]]
        for row,i in enumerate(selected):
            vals = [G[row,j] for j in core if selected[j] != i]
            print(nm(i), f"mean core cosine={np.mean(vals):.3f}",
                  f"min={np.min(vals):.3f}")

    print("\nEarly-five differences after removing their shared dominant modes:")
    core = families["early-five"]
    u, s, vt = svd(templates["early-five"], full_matrices=False)
    U, V = u[:,:4], vt[:4].T
    residuals = []
    for i in core:
        M = H[i]["M"]
        shared = U @ (U.T @ M @ V) @ V.T
        residuals.append(M-shared)
        print(nm(i), "shared squared-norm fraction",
              round(float(np.sum(shared**2)/np.sum(M**2)), 3))
    print("residual-score cosines; columns", ",".join(nm(i) for i in core))
    for i,r in zip(core,residuals):
        print(nm(i), np.round([cosine(r,t) for t in residuals], 3))

            F = np.sqrt(max(np.sum(Gq * Gk), 1e-30))

    mf = M.reshape(144, -1)
    tf = T.reshape(144, -1)
    mn = np.linalg.norm(mf, axis=1)
    tn = np.linalg.norm(tf, axis=1)
    G = (mf @ mf.T) / (mn[:, None] * mn[None, :])

    # Separate symmetric matching structure from antisymmetric ordering structure.
    S = (M + M.transpose(0, 2, 1)).reshape(144, -1)
    sn = np.linalg.norm(S, axis=1)
    GS = (S @ S.T) / (sn[:, None] * sn[None, :])
    del S
    A = (M - M.transpose(0, 2, 1)).reshape(144, -1)
    an = np.linalg.norm(A, axis=1)
    GA = (A @ A.T) / (an[:, None] * an[None, :])
    del A

    # <QK^T, VO> equals the trace of the key-side composed circuit.
    C = (mf @ tf.T) / (mn[:, None] * tn[None, :])
    B = np.stack(bs)
    bn = np.linalg.norm(B, axis=1)
    GB = (B @ B.T) / (bn[:, None] * bn[None, :])

    print("Connected families of similar score matrices (positive cosine edges):")
    for label, Gx, thresholds in [
        ("full", G, [0.65, 0.45, 0.30]),
        ("antisymmetric", GA, [0.65, 0.45]),
        ("symmetric", GS, [0.65]),
    ]:
        for threshold in thresholds:
            count, labels = connected_components(Gx > threshold, directed=False)
            groups = [np.flatnonzero(labels == k) for k in range(count)]
            groups = [x for x in groups if len(x) > 1]
            print(label, threshold, "; ".join(
                ",".join(name(i) for i in x) for x in groups) or "(none)")

    print("\nFor each head:")
    print("Q: two nearest full-score matrices; A: nearest antisymmetric part;")
    print("B: nearest source-bias direction; K<-: strongest positive earlier VO alignment.")
    print("All numbers are cosines, not measured attention behavior.")
    for i in range(144):
        q = G[i].copy()
        a = GA[i].copy()
        bb = GB[i].copy()
        q[i] = a[i] = bb[i] = -np.inf
        js = np.argsort(q)[-2:][::-1]
        ja, jb = np.argmax(a), np.argmax(bb)
        earlier = (i//12)*12
        if earlier:
            jc = np.argmax(C[i, :earlier])
            ctxt = f"{name(jc)}:{C[i,jc]:.3f}"
        else:
            ctxt = "-"
        print(f"{name(i):5} Q {name(js[0])}:{q[js[0]]:.3f} "
              f"{name(js[1])}:{q[js[1]]:.3f} "
              f"A {name(ja)}:{a[ja]:.3f} B {name(jb)}:{bb[jb]:.3f} K<- {ctxt}")

    print("\nStrongest earlier-output / later-key matching alignments:")
    edges = [(float(C[i,j]), i, j) for i in range(144)
             for j in range((i//12)*12)]
    for value, i, j in sorted(edges, reverse=True)[:35]:
        print(f"{name(j)} -> keys of {name(i)}: {value:.4f}")
